questions.title: Round a size up safely
questions.prompt: Round bytes up to the next multiple of alignment. alignment must be positive; throw std::invalid_argument for zero. Throw std::overflow_error if the rounded result cannot fit in uint64_t. Alignment need not be a power of two.

tests.label: Already aligned
tests.hint: Do not add a full alignment when the remainder is zero.

tests.label: Non-power-of-two
tests.hint: Bit masks are insufficient for arbitrary alignments.

tests.label: Zero alignment
tests.hint: Reject zero before using the remainder operator.

tests.label: Overflow
tests.hint: Check the available range before adding.

hints: Compare bytes with max - extra before computing bytes + extra.
questions.explanation: Checking before addition avoids unsigned wraparound. This function calculates a size; it does not itself allocate or align a memory address.

questions.title: Repair an overflow-prone bounds check
questions.prompt: Return whether length bytes starting at offset fit in a buffer of size bytes. An empty range at size is allowed. Avoid addition that can wrap around size_t.
questions.signature: bool fits(std::size_t offset, std::size_t length, std::size_t size)

tests.label: Exact end
tests.hint: A range may end exactly at size.

tests.label: Too long
tests.hint: The remaining space is only two bytes.

tests.label: Empty at end
tests.hint: An empty range at the end is allowed.

tests.label: Offset outside
tests.hint: Validate the offset even when length is zero.

tests.label: Wraparound attack
tests.hint: Do not let offset+length wrap into a small value.

hints: First check that offset is no greater than size.
Only then is size-offset safe to compute.
questions.explanation: The && operator evaluates its right side only after the left side is true. That makes the subtraction safe and avoids overflow-prone addition.

questions.title: Advance a partial transfer
questions.prompt: Track a transfer of requested bytes. completed is the old count and reported is the new chunk length. Return the new count. Throw std::invalid_argument if the old count is too large or the chunk exceeds the remaining space.
questions.signature: std::size_t advance(std::size_t completed, std::size_t reported, std::size_t requested)

tests.label: Partial chunk
tests.hint: Add the new chunk to the completed count.

tests.label: Finish exactly
tests.hint: Completion at the requested count is valid.

tests.label: No progress
tests.hint: A zero-sized chunk leaves the count unchanged.

tests.label: Invalid old state
tests.hint: Check the old count before subtracting it.

hints: Check the chunk against the remaining amount before addition.
questions.explanation: This is the accounting rule used around partial reads or writes. It does not perform I/O; it gives a small, testable boundary for real I/O code.
questions.chapterTitle: Performing Low-Level File and Device I/O
